diarrhoea_grade.label: Current diarrhoea grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Increase of 7 or more stools per day above baseline, incontinence, hospital care indicated, or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: Count stools per day above the patient's baseline. Assess ostomy output, continence, hydration, fever, abdominal pain, sepsis and whether hospital care is indicated. Compare with the patient’s baseline stool/stoma output; record current versus worst episode grade, fever, neutropenia and occurrence separately.
diarrhoea_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP 00691 provides dose-management rows, not a complete grading table. CTCAE v 5.0 descriptions are a grading aid; source-specific dose thresholds, persistence and recurrence remain authoritative.

hand_foot_grade.label: Current hand-foot syndrome grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No palmar–plantar erythrodysesthesia.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Minimal skin changes or dermatitis, such as erythema, oedema or hyperkeratosis, without pain.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Painful skin changes, including peeling, blisters, bleeding, fissures, oedema or hyperkeratosis; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

hand_foot_grade.assessment_guidance: Inspect palms and soles for erythema, oedema, hyperkeratosis, peeling, fissures or blisters; assess pain and functional impact.
